theory.intro: A **cyclic quadrilateral** is a four-sided shape whose vertices all lie on one circle. Each side is a chord, so the circle's angle properties fix two relationships between its angles.
steps: Identify which two angles are opposite each other, or identify the exterior angle and the interior angle opposite that vertex.
Decide which property applies: opposite angles supplementary, or exterior angle equals the opposite interior angle.
Write the equation from the property.

foundation.solution_text:
$\angle BCD = 180^{\circ} - \angle DAB$ (opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary)
$x = 180^{\circ} - 105^{\circ} = 75^{\circ}$
$\angle CDA = 180^{\circ} - \angle ABC$
$y = 180^{\circ} - 100^{\circ} = 80^{\circ}$

$\angle DCE = \angle DAB$ (exterior angle of a cyclic quadrilateral equals the opposite interior angle)
$x = 95^{\circ}$

$\angle BCD = 180^{\circ} - \angle DCE$ (angles on a straight line $BE$)
$x = 180^{\circ} - 110^{\circ} = 70^{\circ}$
$\angle DAB = \angle DCE$ (exterior angle equals the opposite interior angle)
$y = 110^{\circ}$

$\angle CDA = 180^{\circ} - \angle ABC$ (opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary)
$x = 180^{\circ} - 100^{\circ} = 80^{\circ}$
Check: $75^{\circ} + 100^{\circ} + 105^{\circ} + 80^{\circ} = 360^{\circ}$ ✓

$\angle DAB + \angle BCD = 180^{\circ}$ (opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary)
$3x + 2x = 180^{\circ}$
$5x = 180^{\circ}$
$x = 36^{\circ}$

In cyclic quadrilateral $ABCD$, $\angle ABC$ and $\angle CDA$ are the two angles that do not share a side.
The angle opposite $\angle ABC$ is $\angle CDA$.

mastery.solution_text:
Let $\angle DAB = \alpha$; this is the angle at the circumference standing on arc $BCD$ (through $C$).
The reflex central angle standing on the same arc is $\angle BOD = 2\alpha$.
Let $\angle BCD = \beta$; this is the angle at the circumference standing on arc $BAD$ (through $A$).
The (non-reflex) central angle standing on the same arc is $\angle BOD = 2\beta$.
The reflex and non-reflex $\angle BOD$ together make a full turn:
$2\alpha + 2\beta = 360^{\circ}$
$\alpha + \beta = 180^{\circ}$
$\therefore \angle DAB + \angle BCD = 180^{\circ}$

$\angle DCB + \angle DCE = 180^{\circ}$ (angles on a straight line $BE$)
$\angle DAB + \angle DCB = 180^{\circ}$ (opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral are supplementary)
Both equations give $180^{\circ} - \angle DCB$, so:
$\angle DCE = 180^{\circ} - \angle DCB = \angle DAB$
$\therefore \angle DCE = \angle DAB$

$\angle BCD = \angle BAE$ (exterior angle equals the opposite interior angle)
$\angle BCD = 65^{\circ}$
$\angle DAB = 180^{\circ} - \angle BAE$ (angles on a straight line $EA$)
$\angle DAB = 180^{\circ} - 65^{\circ} = 115^{\circ}$
$\angle ABC = \angle ADF$ (exterior angle equals the opposite interior angle)
$\angle ABC = 92^{\circ}$
$\angle CDA = 180^{\circ} - \angle ADF$ (angles on a straight line $CF$)
$\angle CDA = 180^{\circ} - 92^{\circ} = 88^{\circ}$
Check: $65^{\circ} + 115^{\circ} + 92^{\circ} + 88^{\circ} = 360^{\circ}$ ✓
